page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6r.4xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by an ARM64 Ampere Altra processor running at 2.8 GHz under the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of memory, delivering a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include support for AES cryptography flags, while advanced instruction sets such as AVX and AMX are not present on the ARM architecture. The instance includes no local storage and does not feature GPU acceleration. Network baseline bandwidth is rated at 5 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluation reveals average overall multi-core performance, evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 28612.3 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9534.0. In memory testing, uncached read bandwidth measures 135.55 GB/sec and write bandwidth measures 69.0 GB/sec. Conversely, single-threaded metrics reflect limitations, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1104.0, a single-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 8.6 GB/sec, and a Passmark encryption score of 2558.55, all positioning in the lower 25th percentile.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM allocation provides a compute-dense execution environment appropriate for multi-threaded workloads. Tested performance highlights capacity for software compilation (Geekbench compilation score of 17034.0), static web serving throughput (18.56 GB/sec), and key-value database operations (22.17 million Redis SET operations/sec). Due to the lack of built-in local SSD storage, deployments requiring persistent data must rely on external network-attached volumes.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6r.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the ARM64 architecture using a 16 vCPU Ampere Altra processor running at 2.8 GHz under KVM virtualization. The system is provisioned with 32.0 GB of memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU, without local storage or GPU accelerators. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps. Benchmark results demonstrate average multi-core CPU performance, software compilation speeds, and static web serving throughput, while single-core processing scores and specialized encryption benchmarks fall into lower performance tiers. With hardware-accelerated AES cryptography support, this server configuration offers resources suited for multi-threaded workloads, static web serving, memory-cached key-value operations like Redis, and small-scale language model execution where local SSD storage is not required.
